summary: Isaiah Berlin was a philosopher who studied at St Paul's School (~1922–1928) and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932). He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from circa 1932 to 1997.

Isaline Blew Horner worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Newnham College and under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held positions at Newnham College, served on Cambridge's Governing Body, and was Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society.

Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishtiaq Hussain Qureshi was a historian and Indologist who studied at St. Stephen's College and the University of Cambridge. He held posts at St. Stephen's College, University of the Punjab, Columbia University, University of Karachi, and the NLPD.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, studying at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College, and Benares Sanskrit College. He held posts at Fort William College, Sanskrit College and University, and was Direktor at Benares Sanskrit College.

Iso Kern is a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Columbia, and National Taiwan University. He held academic posts at KU Leuven, Heidelberg, Bern, Zurich, and Fribourg.
Issaen Ikeyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1976, he was attested as holding professorial posts at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji Junior College.
Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed studies at Sophia University and a master's program at Aichi Gakuin University.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University. She held a post at the University of Washington and taught Qian Lin.

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1858–1862). He held a post at the university's Faculty of Oriental Studies (~1871–1890) and taught Fyodor Shcherbatskoy.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist scholar who studied at the University of Saint Petersburg, as well as under Albrecht Weber and Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev. He served as a professor at the University of Saint Petersburg.

Ives Goddard was a linguist who studied at Harvard College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1963–1969). He held positions at Harvard University (~1966–1976), the National Museum of Natural History (~1976), and the Smithsonian Institution (~1976).
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa (1970–1988). He taught David P. Jackson.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned her PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp. She held a dissertation completion and lectureship fellowship at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a lecturer at the University of Prague in 1960 and held a post at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology in 1970.

Iwao Nakajima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hitotsubashi University and under Nikki Kimura. He held a post at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and served as head at Sandhaan around 1999.

Iwao Shima was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Nagoya University (~1970–1979). He spent his career at Kanazawa University (~1988–1999), serving as professor from circa 1999 to 2007.

Izumi Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1987–1997). She held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as assistant professor (1997) and director (2019–2023).
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She held a post at the University of Washington and taught Qian Lin.
